liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Box of Rain** (1 review): Reviewer finds Box of Rain warm and rich, despite disliking Phil's singing [14]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the best Row Jimmy they have heard, smooth and rich [11]
- **Playin' in the Band** (1 review): After the second chorus Jerry switches on the wah-wah; the jam wanders through several grooves and runs about twenty minutes [9]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Encore Sugar Magnolia sounds as if Garcia plays pedal steel, with slide and open-string fumbling early before settling into leads [16]

## The recordings

- **gd73-03-16.sbd.hamilton-jackson.167.14770.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 204 min; rated 4.57/5 by 30 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the overall sound very good, with Garcia's guitar tone especially striking; The mix takes about a song and a half to settle, then sounds very good [7][8]
- **gd1973-03-16.sbd.cantor.hamilton.167.shnf**: soundboard; 25 songs; 204 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: Flaws come from typical 1973 sound system problems and waterlogged set 1 reels, including a Big River dropout and a Truckin' splice [2]
- **gd1973-03-16.sbd.miller.79186.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 195 min; rated 4.37/5 by 19 [4]. Said about its sound: This version avoids flaws of other sources and improves sound quality, though Sugar Magnolia has some static [4]
- **gd1973-03-16.152003.SonyStereo.ECM.Moskal.t.flac16**: source not stated; 26 songs; 191 min [6]. Said about its sound: Flaws include a tape flip in Playin', missing Dark Star intro, and degraded quality for the Sugar Magnolia encore [6]

## Around the show

- Banter before Looks Like Rain: fans threw joints on stage and Jerry asked them to stop and just smoke [12]
- Bill Graham's introduction before China Cat names the band's home state, California, rather than a city [18]
- Uploader calls this the infamous bust show [4]
- Billed as a dance concert; Sons of Champlin did not play after the singer's father died, so New Riders opened [6]
- Reviewer ranks this show, with the 22nd at Utica, as favorites of the five-night New York run [9]
- Reviewer says the band never opened a show so sharply, and recommends this version over the following one [11]
- Quality is better than Moskal's 3-15 recording the night before, with an improved mix [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd73-03-16.sbd.hamilton-jackson.167.14770.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Set 1 is Betty Cantor master stereo recording via PCM, DAT, CDR; set 2 from reel via DAT, CD; extracted by G.S. Hamilton [1]
- **gd1973-03-16.sbd.cantor.hamilton.167.shnf**: transferred by James Warner and G. S. Hamilton; source: Set 1: Betty MSR > PCM > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN and Set 2: MSR > Reel > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN [2]
- **gd1973-03-16.sbd.miller.79186.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Set 1: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat (44.1k) DSet 2: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (44.1k) D [4]. Also: Taken from a DAT; Dark Star from 18:10 through Morning Dew comes from the same source as set 1 [4]
- **gd1973-03-16.152003.SonyStereo.ECM.Moskal.t.flac16**: taped by Gerry Moskal; transferred by Gerry Moskal & Brian Mandel; source: Sony Stereo ECM -->SONY TCD126 Location: TBD [6]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum - March 16, 1973](https://www.dead.net/show/march-16-1973) [20]
